_comment: Canonical tier and group definitions, shared by every status hub. Kept here rather than duplicated into each hub's status.json so three copies can't drift apart — a tier's promise is a claim made on ~24 public repos and it has to read the same everywhere.

Active.oneLiner: shipping now; installable today and still gaining capability
Active.promise: I'm in this most weeks. Features are landing, so expect breaking changes between releases — read the changelog before you upgrade. I read issues and generally act on them quickly.

Building.oneLiner: under construction; nothing released, nothing promised
Building.promise: Being built. Nothing is released, nothing is supported, and it can change shape or disappear without notice. Don't build on it — watch the repo if you want to know when it ships.

Maintained.oneLiner: feature-complete; kept working and patched, not grown
Maintained.promise: I'm not adding features here. It still gets security patches, dependency bumps and fixes for anything that breaks. Safe to depend on for exactly what it does today.

Parked.oneLiner: done or paused; it works, nothing is watching it
Parked.promise: Finished or paused. It does what the README says and I left it working, but nothing is watching it, so it could rot quietly. I'll answer a question. I'm not promising a fix or a release.

Unmaintained.promise: I'm not watching this one. Something it advertises may already be broken, and bugs won't be fixed on a schedule. Read it, fork it, vendor it — this says nothing about whether the code is any good.

Reference.oneLiner: content, not software; graded on how current it is
Reference.promise: The content was accurate as of the date shown. Links and details go stale.

Fork.oneLiner: someone else's project; the real one is upstream
Fork.promise: Not my project and not maintained by me. The canonical version is upstream — go there for issues, releases and support.

Archived.promise: Archived on GitHub and read-only. Kept so links don't rot.
